content: L2/cross-chain bridge patterns: (1) lock-and-mint -- source-chain contract escrows the canonical asset, destination mints a wrapped representation; reverse burns the wrapped asset and releases escrow. (2) burn-and-mint -- source burns, destination mints, no persistent escrow (used when both sides recognize the same canonical asset authority). Canonical L2 bridges lock on L1 and mint on L2, inheriting L1 finality/security but incurring withdrawal-delay/challenge-period latency on the way back. Escrow/vault contracts are the most attractive attack target in lock-and-mint since compromise there can double-spend the wrapped supply -- the security-critical invariant is that minted supply on the destination side must never exceed what's actually escrowed/burned on the source side.
